messages.subject: DIF testing with 2 factors
parts:
Hi Phil. 


I appreciate your help from the last time. Currently, I have another question and I apologize in advance if this is a basic question. I'm trying to conduct a DIF analysis in a model with 2 factors. I'm testing DIF in a compensatory confirmatory model. However, when I'm using the function DIF I've got a negative LL difference:

$i13                                                               
           AIC     AICc    SABIC      BIC    logLik                 X2  df   p   
 1 113365.6 113679.5 114299.4 115652.8 -56256.79      NaN NaN NaN    
 2 113508.5 113825.9 114446.8 115806.4 -56326.25 -138.932   2   1 


My question is the following: can the function DIF conduct this analysis in a multidimensional model? 

This is my code:


mod1 <- mirt.model('F1 = 1-11,18, 20-40,42-65,66,67-71
                    F2 = 12-17,19,41
                    ')


configural <- multipleGroup(dat.2[,7:77], model =  mod1, as.character(dat.2[,"SWD"]), itemtype = '3PL', method = 'MHRM')


##Factor 1
dif <- DIF(configural,c('a1','d'),  plotdif = TRUE, Wald = TRUE), items2test = c(1:11, 18, 20:40, 42:65,66,67:71))

##Factor 2

dif2 <- DIF(configural,c('a2','d'), plotdif = TRUE, items2test = c(12:17,19,41))

I can also send you my data set if that helps to answer my question.


Thank you again for your kindly help, and thank you for your amazing package.

Best wishes.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: DIF testing with 2 factors
parts:
It's also possible this is a local minimum issue, because the 3PLM is known to have trouble converging (also this model doesn't seem to free the latent variances in the focal group). But yes seeing the data would make it easier to track down what is going on. Cheers.

Phil
